_note: Bypass-resistance set for abusive language across TR/EN/RU. Written before the stems were extended. The 'safe' half is the important half: Turkish normalisation folds ş→s, so a stem like 'sik' endangers 'şikayet' (complaint) — one of the commonest words on a campus app — and 'göt' endangers 'götürmek' (to take). A profanity filter that refuses ordinary words gets switched off, and then it protects nobody.

_untargeted_note: These publish, and that is a POLICY choice rather than a detection failure — the engine matches every one of these roots, then declines to act because nobody is being sworn at. The corpus (ModerationCorpusTest, 150 labelled cases) settles the same question the same way for 'What the fuck is wrong with this system?', 'Какого хуя эта система не работает?' and 'Amına koyayım böyle sistemin.' No rule can refuse the list below and still publish those three; they are the same speech act. If the university wants coarse language held regardless of target, that is one switch in decideFromWords() — and it will hold student complaints about the app along with it. Listed separately so the decision stays visible instead of hiding inside a pass rate.
